extracted.intended_audience: NLP/ML researchers and engineers building or evaluating LLM-based story evaluators and story generation systems
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, training, and evaluating an LLM-based story evaluator (reward model) that outputs score-aligned Chain-of-Thought rationales for pairwise story comparisons and can be used to guide story generation via RL. Focuses on multi-aspect scoring, CoT synthesis/evolution, and use as a reward model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pairwise comparison format
rubrics_metrics.description: Use pairwise comparison (evaluating two stories Sa, Sb together) rather than pointwise scoring, because pairwise comparison exhibits significantly higher rating consistency and captures nuanced human preferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The framework is grounded in pairwise comparison; training and data synthesis produce pairs with score-aligned CoT. Empirical claim: pairwise CoT significantly outperforms pointwise CoT across models and datasets (see ablation and Table 3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-dimensional evaluation aspects and score range
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate stories across multiple aspects k (examples: Creativity, Surprise) and produce per-aspect scores ya,k and yb,k with y ∈ [1,5].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aspects are weighted by αk in the reward function. The evaluator must handle K aspects and produce per-aspect numeric scores; datasets (HANNA/StoryER/OpenMEVA) provide multi-dimensional annotations used for training and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Score-aligned Chain-of-Thought (CoT) rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: The evaluator should output, for a pair and an aspect k, a textual rationale Ck that logically justifies the assigned scores: Rϕ(Sa, Sb, k) = (Ck; ya,k; yb,k).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training data tuples are (Sa, Sb, k, Ck, ya,k, yb,k). CoTs must be aligned with the final numeric judgments and provide step-by-step reasoning to improve fidelity and explainability.

rubrics_metrics.name: CoT logical consistency (Self-Rulecheck)
rubrics_metrics.description: A CoT must have a final conclusion explicitly consistent with the ground-truth scores; the pipeline applies a deterministic ParseScores(·) to extract final scores from the CoT and checks equality with targets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operator Frule: CoT passes only if extracted scores (y') exactly match ground truth (y*). This is applied at multiple stages (e.g., initial rule-check and a subsequent rule-check after refinement).

rubrics_metrics.name: CoT clarity and improved reasoning flow (Self-Refinement)
rubrics_metrics.description: CoTs should be refined to improve logical flow and clarity while preserving the original reasoning and final conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operator Frefine uses a refinement agent (Arefine) to produce C'i,k from Ci,k; refined candidates replace originals for subsequent filtering. Emphasize preserving original reasoning content while enhancing readability and structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: CoT robustness via adversarial contradiction detection (Self-Attack)
rubrics_metrics.description: A CoT is robust if, when the final scores are altered to contradict its rationale, the model (acting as a judge) detects the inconsistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operator Fattack: create corrupted version with contradictory final scores and prompt the model (agent Aattack) to detect the contradiction. CoTs that fail to expose the injected contradiction are filtered out.

rubrics_metrics.name: CoT confidence selection (Self-Confidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Select CoTs that lead the model to predict the ground-truth scores with high confidence: the logit corresponding to the ground-truth score must be maximal for each story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operator Fconfidence inspects model logits L(y|S, C) and requires argmax_y L = y* for Sa and Sb. This ensures selected CoTs support confident model predictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-persona CoT synthesis for diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: Synthesize CoTs using a multi-persona strategy where each persona (e.g., academic, artistic, sharp-tongued) generates candidate derivations to foster diverse reasoning styles and viewpoints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define a set of personas P = {p1,...,pm} and prompt LLMself with each persona to produce candidate (Cm_k; ya,k; yb,k), forming a large Dpool of diverse derivations; diversity helps cover varied human perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: CoT evolution & selection pipeline sequencing
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply a multistage evolutionary selection pipeline (P = [Frule, Frefine, Frule, Fattack, Fconfidence]) to filter noisy synthetic CoTs and produce a high-quality final pool Dfinal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates must survive every operator in sequence; refinement operators modify CoTs (and Frule re-checks consistency post-refinement). The pipeline is algorithmically specified (Algorithm 1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Parseable numeric scoring in CoT
rubrics_metrics.description: CoTs must contain an explicit, parseable final score statement so a deterministic ParseScores function can extract numeric scores for rule-checking and downstream use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoring tokens must be unambiguous (e.g., '[1, 3]') so automatic parsing and Frule can deterministically validate alignment between rationale and numeric labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reward composition for generation (Radv, Rabs, Rlen)
rubrics_metrics.description: When using the evaluator as a reward model, compute reward as R(Si, Sgt) = Radv + Rabs + Rlen, combining relative advantage, absolute quality, and length reward components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Radv measures improvement over a group reference (weighted sum of yi,k − ygt,k), Rabs measures absolute scores (weighted sum of yi,k), and Rlen is a length-based term w3·f(len(Si)). Weights w1,w2,w3 and aspect weights αk modulate importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a stable high-quality anchor reference (Sgt)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute relative advantage and some reward terms against a pre-generated, high-quality reference story Sgt (anchor) to provide a stable baseline for rewards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sgt is generated from the base model and serves as a common comparator across candidate group {S1...SG} sampled by the policy for GRPO updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aspect weighting in reward (αk) and hyperparameters (wj)
rubrics_metrics.description: Control the importance of each evaluation aspect via weights αk and tune global reward component weights w1,w2,w3 to shape generator optimization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designers must set αk to reflect relative priority of aspects (e.g., Surprise vs Coherence) and choose wj to balance relative vs absolute vs length incentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: GRPO training objective and safe optimization
rubrics_metrics.description: Optimize policy with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO): use group-level advantage ˆAi = ri − (1/G) sum rj, apply token-level policy ratios ρi,t, clipping (clip(ρ,1−ϵ,1+ϵ)), and a KL penalty −β DKL(πθ || πref).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement token-level advantages (ˆAi,t = ˆAi), clipping, and KL control to limit policy drift; be aware of reward hacking risks when applying RL to open-ended generation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation metrics for evaluator accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess agreement between model-predicted ratings and human judgments using Pearson correlation (r), Spearman rank correlation (ρ), Kendall's τ, Mean Squared Error (MSE) on normalized scores, and F1-Score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report multiple correlation coefficients (↑ better) and MSE (↓ better) to provide complementary views of correlation, ranking, and absolute accuracy; follow prior-work protocols (e.g., Coke).

rubrics_metrics.name: Human evaluation protocol for generated stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Use expert human judges (panel of four professional screenwriters) who rate generated stories on a 1–5 scale across six dimensions: Relevance, Coherence, Empathy, Surprise, Engagement, and Complexity. Report Average Score and Win Rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Average Score: mean across six dimensions for each model. Win Rate: head-to-head comparisons against baseline generated stories and human dataset stories. Use domain experts for nuanced judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: No-reference / reference-free evaluation preference
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer evaluators that do not require a ground-truth reference text, since creative scenarios often lack a single correct reference and reference-based methods are impractical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper emphasizes that models like TIGERScore/InstructScore requiring references are constrained; EvolvR is reference-free and thus more applicable to open-ended creative evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use official dataset splits and zero-shot generalization testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow official train/test splits for benchmarks (StoryER, HANNA) to ensure reproducibility; report zero-shot performance on additional benchmarks (OpenMEVA) to evaluate generalization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to publicly released splits; include cross-dataset zero-shot tests because OpenMEVA uses a single holistic score and is a more challenging generalization check.

rubrics_metrics.name: Component ablation and incremental validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Validate the contribution of system components (multi-persona, rule-check, refinement agent, attack agent, confidence agent) via incremental ablation studies to quantify each module's effect on correlation metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct controlled experiments adding components one-by-one and report Pearson/Spearman/Kendall to demonstrate individual and synergistic gains (see Table 6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid reward hacking and monitor optimization artifacts
rubrics_metrics.description: When applying RL (GRPO) with evaluator rewards, monitor for reward hacking and limited performance gains; careful reward engineering and evaluation are required to prevent optimization shortcuts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper notes GRPO applied directly to base models yields limited gains in some cases due to reward hacking; include diagnostics and safeguards in RL training.
